description: Income tax and other government payments

entries.name: Alaska Department of Revenue - Tax Division (no individual income tax)
entries.service_area_detail: Alaska has no state individual income tax or statewide sales tax; seniors typically owe only local property/sales taxes (borough/city)
entries.mail_payment_address: Tax Division, Alaska Department of Revenue, P.O. Box 110420, Juneau, AK 99811-0420
entries.notes: Included for completeness: no individual income tax. Property tax bills are local (borough/municipality). Senior property tax exemption (first $150,000 assessed value, age 65+) is administered by local assessors, not the Tax Division.

entries.name: Alabama Department of Revenue (individual income tax)
entries.service_area_detail: Alabama individual income tax balances, billing letters/assessments, 40ES estimated payments
entries.phone_customer_service: 334-353-8096 (Taxpayer Assistance Group; also regional Taxpayer Service Centers listed on Help Center)
entries.mail_payment_address: Billing letters/assessments: mail to the address on the letter (per Income Tax Payment Options page)
entries.payment_processor: My Alabama Taxes (MAT, state portal) - ACH debit and credit/debit card
entries.senior_programs: Homestead exemptions for age 65+ (income-based: AGI under $12,000 exempt from all ad valorem taxes; otherwise state exemption plus $2,000 county assessed-value exemption); apply at county office: https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/property-tax/homestead-exemptions.
entries.notes: Pay a Bill link on MAT requires the Letter ID and Account Number from the bill. Income tax payment options: https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/individual-corporate/income-tax-payment-options/. EFT/ACH: https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/individual-corporate/pay-by-eft-ach/. Form 40ES vouchers for estimated tax. MAT EFT payments can be cancelled the same day by 4:00 p.m. CT while Pending (click request > Withdraw > Confirm).

entries.name: City of Birmingham Tax and License Division - Occupational Tax
entries.service_area_detail: Birmingham occupational tax on wages and self-employment earnings for work done in the city (withheld by employers; self-employed file directly)
entries.senior_programs: The occupational tax applies only to earnings from work done in Birmingham; retirees with only Social Security or pension income owe nothing.
entries.notes: File and pay the occupational tax online through the city's HdL tax portal (https://birminghamal.hdlgov.com/Home/Home/Taxes); online filing is the city's preferred method and the city has discontinued the mail payment option for these taxes. Office: City Hall, Room TL-100, 710 North 20th Street, Birmingham, AL 35203.

entries.name: City of Gadsden Revenue Department (occupational tax and business licenses)
entries.service_area_detail: Gadsden occupational tax on earnings from work done in the city, and business licenses
entries.mail_payment_address: City of Gadsden Revenue Department, P.O. Box 267, Gadsden, AL 35902
entries.senior_programs: The occupational tax applies only to earnings from work in Gadsden, not to Social Security or pensions.
entries.notes: Business license applications and renewals are handled online (https://gadsden-al.tekconnectgov.com/). Mail: P.O. Box 267, Gadsden, AL 35902. Call the Revenue Department about occupational tax for self-employment earnings in Gadsden.

entries.name: Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration - Individual Income Tax
entries.service_area_detail: Arkansas individual income tax balances and estimated payments (AR1000ES)
entries.payment_processor: ATAP (Arkansas Taxpayer Access Point, state GenTax portal) for ACH; ACI Payments (officialpayments.com) for credit/debit card
entries.senior_programs: Homestead property tax credit and assessment freeze for homeowners 65+ or disabled (apply with county assessor): https://www.dfa.arkansas.gov/office/arkansas-assessment-coordination-division/real-property/property-tax-relief/.
entries.notes: Credit card payments: https://www.dfa.arkansas.gov/office/taxes/income-tax-administration/individual-income-tax/credit-card-payments/ (ACI Payments, fee). ATAP lets users view payments submitted, recent account activity and correspondence, and store banking info. Payment vouchers: https://www.dfa.arkansas.gov/office/taxes/income-tax-administration/payment-vouchers/.

entries.name: American Samoa Government - Department of Treasury Tax Office
entries.service_area_detail: American Samoa territorial income tax (Form 390 filings); in-person filing season from late January.
entries.notes: Form 390 spreadsheets by year are available; filing-season hours Mon-Fri 8am-3pm.

entries.name: Arizona Department of Revenue (individual income tax)
entries.service_area_detail: Arizona individual income tax balances, 140ES estimated payments, payment arrangements
entries.mail_payment_address: Mail with Form AZ-140V payment voucher to the address on the form (https://azdor.gov/forms/payment-vouchers)
entries.payment_processor: AZTaxes.gov (state portal) - free e-check; credit/debit card (fee)
entries.senior_programs: Property Tax Refund (Credit) Claim, Form 140PTC (refundable credit for qualified low-income homeowners/renters; see form instructions for age 65+/income limits): https://azdor.gov/forms/tax-credits-forms/property-tax-refund-credit-claim-form-fillable.
entries.notes: E-check payments can be scheduled for a later date and are free; scheduled e-payments can be canceled at AZTaxes "Cancel Payment" (Individual). Estimated payments due Apr 15, Jun 15, Sep 15, Jan 15. Payment plan request online at https://www.aztaxes.gov/Home/PaymentPlan (confirmation number and monthly amount given; may take up to 8 weeks if no bill yet). Paper payment info: https://azdor.gov/making-payments-late-payments-and-filing-extensions. Property Tax Refund Credit (Form 140PTC) for low-income seniors 65+ is claimed on the state return. Cancel Individual Income Payment page (https://www.aztaxes.gov/Home/CancelPaymentIndividual/) cancels e-filed/AZTaxes payments until 5pm MST the business day before withdrawal; needs confirmation number, SSN, ZIP, tax year and amount.

entries.name: California Franchise Tax Board (FTB) - personal income tax
entries.service_area_detail: California personal income tax balances, bills/notices, Form 540-ES estimated payments, payment plans
entries.phone_customer_service: Payment plans 800-689-4776; manage/skip plan payment 888-635-0494 (general line not captured in fetched text)
entries.mail_payment_address: Estimated payments: Franchise Tax Board, PO Box 942867, Sacramento CA 94267-0008 (with Form 540-ES voucher; check payable to "Franchise Tax Board")
entries.payment_processor: FTB Web Pay (free bank debit, state); ACI Payments (officialpayments.com) for credit card; FTB mobile app
entries.senior_programs: Senior Citizens' Property Tax Postponement is run by the State Controller (not FTB). FTB Taxpayer Advocate: https://www.ftb.ca.gov/help/disagree-or-resolve-an-issue/taxpayer-advocate-services.html.
entries.notes: Web Pay (https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/bank-account/index.asp) can schedule payments up to one year ahead; cancel a Web Pay request up to 2 business days before the scheduled date (help page). MyFTB account shows balance, lets you view/cancel/schedule payments. Credit card: https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/credit-card.html. Estimated tax: https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/estimated-tax-payments.html. If you cannot pay: https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/if-you-cant-pay/index.html. Payment plans have automatic monthly bank withdrawal option; manage online. FTB credit card page (https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/credit-card.html) says pay online or call 800-272-9829 with ACI Payments (2.3% fee).

entries.name: City and County of Denver Occupational Privilege Tax (OPT) - Treasury Division
entries.service_area_detail: Denver employees earning $500+ a month in Denver pay $5.75/month (withheld); employers and self-employed owners/partners pay $4.00/month per person, with no earnings threshold for owners
entries.senior_programs: The OPT applies only to people working in Denver; Social Security and pension income are not involved. A retiree who still runs a small business in Denver owes the $4.00/month owner portion. Denver's Senior Property Tax Exemption is a separate program (https://www.denvergov.org/My-Property/Property-Tax/Senior-Property-Tax-Exemption).
entries.notes: Employees' OPT is withheld by the employer, so wage earners get no bill. Self-employed owners and partners file and pay the OPT in the eBiz Tax Center (https://www.denvergov.org/ebiztax/_/) by e-check or card (2.5% fee), by mailed check, or in person at Taxpayer Services.

entries.name: Colorado Department of Revenue - Taxation (individual income tax)
entries.service_area_detail: Colorado individual income tax bills, estimated payments, payment plans
entries.payment_processor: Revenue Online (state) - credit/debit card or e-check, no login required; EFT; check; cash
entries.senior_programs: PTC Rebate (Property Tax/Rent/Heat Rebate for seniors 65+, surviving spouses, disabled) is available through Colorado tax.
entries.notes: Pay Tax Bill page lists card/e-check, check, EFT, cash methods. Payment Options by tax type: https://tax.colorado.gov/payment-options. Estimated payments page explains Revenue Online and EFT (EFT requires advance registration). Payment plans: https://tax.colorado.gov/payment-plan. Citizens advocate: https://tax.colorado.gov/citizens-advocate.

entries.name: Connecticut Department of Revenue Services (DRS) - individual income tax
entries.service_area_detail: Connecticut income tax balances, CT-1040ES estimated payments
entries.payment_processor: myconneCT (state portal, ACH debit/direct payment); credit/debit card via card service provider (convenience fee)
entries.senior_programs: Renters' Rebate Program for elderly (65+) and disabled renters (CT OPM): https://portal.ct.gov/opm/igpp/grants/tax-relief-grants/renters--rebate-for-elderly-disabled-renters-tax-relief-program.
entries.notes: Tax Information page (Payment Options and Estimated Tax Payments sections) explains ACH debit and card payments via myconneCT; 2026 estimated due Apr 15, Jun 15, Sep 15, Jan 15 2027. myconneCT FAQ: https://portal.ct.gov/drs/myconnect/myconnect-2/faq.

entries.name: DC Office of Tax and Revenue (OTR) - individual income tax
entries.service_area_detail: District of Columbia individual income tax (D-40) balances, estimated payments (D-40ES), installment agreements; also real property tax
entries.mail_payment_address: Check/money order payable to "DC Treasurer" with TIN, phone and tax year; mailing address per form
entries.payment_processor: MyTax.DC.gov (state portal): ACH debit free; credit/debit card 2.25% convenience fee
entries.senior_programs: Taxpayer Advocate: https://otr.cfo.dc.gov/page/taxpayer-advocate; real property tax payment/billing: https://otr.cfo.dc.gov/page/real-property-payments-billing.
entries.notes: Installment agreements are set up in MyTax.DC.gov with mandatory automatic ACH debit (bank info required) - effectively autopay; generally <=24 months and balance < $100,000. Estimated tax interest rules: https://otr.cfo.dc.gov/page/underpayment-estimated-tax-interest.

entries.name: City of Wilmington Earned Income (Wage) Tax - Department of Finance
entries.service_area_detail: Wilmington residents and people who work in Wilmington: city earned income (wage) tax and net profits tax
entries.notes: The City of Wilmington Department of Finance collects the city wage tax (withheld by employers) and net profits tax from self-employed residents and workers.

entries.name: Delaware Division of Revenue - personal income tax
entries.service_area_detail: Delaware personal income tax balances, delinquent bills, quarterly estimated tax
entries.phone_customer_service: 302-577-8200 (Personal Income Tax Assistance); Collections/Account Management 302-577-8785; Installments 302-577-8586
entries.senior_programs: Senior School Property Tax Credit (65+, 50% of school property tax on primary residence, capped; apply by April 30): https://finance.delaware.gov/senior-relief/.
entries.notes: Individuals can pay a current return balance or delinquent bill, and quarterly estimated tax, on the Delaware Taxpayer Portal. Installment agreements handled by phone (302-577-8586). Individual Taxpayer Services hub: https://revenue.delaware.gov/individual-taxpayer-services/.

entries.name: Florida Department of Revenue (no personal income tax)
entries.service_area_detail: No personal income tax; property tax info only
entries.senior_programs: Homestead exemption and additional senior (65+, limited income) homestead exemptions - applied for with the county property appraiser.
entries.notes: No state personal income tax. Seniors' main state/local tax bill is the property tax, billed and collected by the county tax collector (not DOR). Included so Florida users see there is no state income tax bill. Exemptions page: https://floridarevenue.com/property/pages/Taxpayers_Exemptions.aspx.

entries.name: Georgia Department of Revenue (individual income tax)
entries.service_area_detail: Georgia individual income tax balances, assessment notices, 500-ES estimated payments, installment agreements
entries.payment_processor: Georgia Tax Center (GTC, state portal) - free bank debit, quick pay without login; credit card/PayPal via third-party processor (2.31% fee, $1 min)
entries.senior_programs: Senior homestead exemptions (65+: $4,000 county exemption with income limit; 62+: $10,000 school exemption and floating inflation-proof exemption); apply at county tax commissioner: https://dor.georgia.gov/property-tax-homestead-exemptions.
entries.notes: Electronic payments can be set up to occur on or before the due date (scheduled). Quick payment: https://dor.georgia.gov/make-quick-payment. Payment FAQ: https://dor.georgia.gov/make-payment-faq. Installment Agreement Request (GA-9465): https://dor.georgia.gov/ga-9465-installment-agreement-request; payment plan default letter explains cancellation: https://dor.georgia.gov/payment-plan-default-letter. Property tax/homestead exemptions (senior) are county-administered. Payment Options page: card/PayPal fee 2.31% ($1 min); credit card payments cannot be canceled once submitted; payment plans via GTC or Form GA-9465; no pay-by-phone line listed. EPayments must be cancelled before 3:00 pm ET on the payment date; credit card payments cannot be cancelled.

entries.name: Guam Department of Revenue and Taxation (DRT) - income tax payments (PayGuam)
entries.service_area_detail: Guam territorial income tax (Guam files instead of the IRS), gross receipts tax and other GovGuam tax bills, paid to the Treasurer of Guam.
entries.mail_payment_address: Dept. of Revenue & Taxation, Taxpayer Services Division, P.O. Box 23607, Barrigada, GU 96921 (general mailing address from the contact page; walk-in 1240 Army Drive, Barrigada)
entries.payment_processor: PayGuam (pay.guam.gov, Government of Guam portal built by Data Management Resources / PacificOne; Visa, MasterCard, Discover, AmEx; registration required)
entries.senior_programs: Guam offers Form 1040-SR (Guam tax return for seniors) on its forms page (https://www.guamtax.com/forms/index.html).
entries.notes: Guamtax.com/help/contact.html is a meta-refresh to /app/contactus.do, which lists phones, the P.O. Box 23607 mailing address and the Barrigada office; phones and mail address are filled from it. MyGuamTax 'How to Pay Your 1040'  walks through paying on Pay.Guam.gov: register, choose 'Income Tax returns', enter the e-filing confirmation details, check out (card only). PayGuam FAQ (https://pay.guam.gov/pg/FAQs.aspx): Visa, MasterCard, Discover, AmEx; PIN-based debit not accepted; income tax/GRT payments need a PIN requested inside PayGuam; 3.50% convenience fee on tax payments since Oct 1, 2024; partial payments allowed; you can pay someone else's bill with their account number and PIN; 'FAST PAY' saves recurring payment details (not automatic payment). Payments list: https://pay.guam.gov/pg/payments.aspx. MyGuamTax individual online services: https://www.myguamtax.com.

entries.name: Hawaii Department of Taxation (individual income tax)
entries.service_area_detail: Hawaii individual income tax balances and N-1 estimated payments
entries.payment_processor: Hawaii Tax Online (HTO, state GenTax portal) - debit payments free; card via third-party processor
entries.senior_programs: Low-income household renters credit is doubled for taxpayers 65+.
entries.notes: E-Services page: https://tax.hawaii.gov/eservices/; About HTO: https://hitax.hawaii.gov/?Link=about. Filing and making debit payments on HTO is free. Payment plans handled by Tax Collection Services (808-587-1600).

entries.name: Iowa Department of Revenue (individual income tax)
entries.service_area_detail: Iowa individual income tax balances, IA 1040ES estimated payments; Iowa Property Tax Credit (seniors/disabled)
entries.payment_processor: GovConnectIowa (state portal) - ACH; credit/debit card (service fee per transaction); check; cash in person
entries.senior_programs: Property Tax Credit Expanded (seniors 65+/disabled, claim 54-001): https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/tax-credits-deductions-exemption/property-tax-credit-expanded; Homestead Tax Credit and Exemption (65+ exemption): https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/property-tax/homestead-tax-credit-and-exemption.
entries.notes: "EasyPay Iowa" page describes card/ACH/check/cash options; misapplied payments 855-314-4692.

entries.name: Idaho State Tax Commission (individual income tax)
entries.service_area_detail: Idaho individual income tax balances, estimated payments, payment plans; property tax relief (circuit breaker) applications
entries.payment_processor: Taxpayer Access Point (TAP, GenTax) - ACH debit free; Quick Pay (no login, no payment history); credit/debit card processed by PayIt (2.5% fee)
entries.senior_programs: Property Tax Reduction (circuit breaker) for homeowners 65+/widowed/disabled - apply in TAP: https://idahotap.gentax.com/TAP?Link=PTR.
entries.notes: Schedule payments in TAP up to a year in advance for individual income tax. Quick Pay: https://idahotap.gentax.com/tap?Link=QuickPay (does not keep payment history). TAP payment plan: https://tax.idaho.gov/online-services/tap/payment-plan/ - payment plans require automatic payments from bank account (autopay). Estimated payment form: https://tax.idaho.gov/document-mngr/forms_EFO00092/.

entries.name: Illinois Department of Revenue (IDOR) - individual income tax
entries.service_area_detail: Illinois individual income tax balances, IL-1040-ES estimated payments, installment payment plans
entries.phone_pay_by_phone: 866-490-2061 (automated pay-by-phone for installment payments, per payment plan page)
entries.mail_payment_address: Installment payments: Installment Contract Unit, Illinois Department of Revenue, PO Box 19035, Springfield, IL 62794-9035
entries.payment_processor: MyTax Illinois (state) - free ACH debit; credit card via Collector Solutions (magic.collectorsolutions.com), 2.25% fee ($1 min)
entries.senior_programs: Senior Citizens Homestead Exemption and Low-Income Senior Citizens Assessment Freeze (county assessor): https://tax.illinois.gov/localgovernments/property/taxrelief.html.
entries.notes: MyTax Illinois lets you file, pay, view balances and manage account. Credit card page: https://tax.illinois.gov/payments/creditcard.html. Payment plan page lists online (MyTax Illinois), card, pay-by-phone and mail options; Form CPP-1 request. IL-PIN FAQ: https://tax.illinois.gov/questionsandanswers/59.html.

entries.name: Indiana Department of Revenue (DOR) - individual income tax
entries.service_area_detail: Indiana individual income tax (incl. county tax) balances, bills, estimated payments, payment plans
entries.payment_processor: INTIME (state GenTax portal) - bank payment free, credit card (fee); guest bill pay with Letter ID
entries.senior_programs: Seniors page: https://www.in.gov/dor/i-am-a/individual/seniors; Unified Tax Credit for the Elderly (IB 26): https://www.in.gov/dor/files/ib26.pdf; Low-income taxpayers: https://www.in.gov/dor/i-am-a/individual/low-income-taxpayers; Taxpayer Advocate Office.
entries.notes: Pay a bill without login via INTIME "Bill payments" panel (needs Letter ID and SSN) - https://intime.dor.in.gov/eServices/?Link=MakePaymentMenu. Estimated tax: https://www.in.gov/dor/i-need-to/make-a-payment/estimated-payments. Payment plan setup guides: https://www.in.gov/dor/files/intime-instructions-payment-plan.pdf and https://www.in.gov/dor/files/intime-guide-payment-plan-payments.pdf.

entries.name: Kansas Department of Revenue (individual income tax)
entries.service_area_detail: Kansas individual income tax balances, estimated tax, delinquent tax debt, payment plans; Homestead refund / SAFESR
entries.payment_processor: Kansas Tax Payment Portal (https://www.kansas.gov/payment-portal/, Kansas.gov) - ACH debit free, credit card (fee); Kansas Customer Service Center for scheduled quarterly payments; debtpay.kdor.ks.gov for delinquent debt
entries.senior_programs: Homestead refund and Property Tax Relief for Low Income Seniors (SAFESR) filed via Individual Income and Homestead e-services: https://www.ksrevenue.gov/eservii.html.
entries.notes: New payment portal cannot schedule future payments; schedule future quarterly estimated payments in the Kansas Customer Service Center (KCSC). Payment plans: $25 administration fee on plans >90 days; request forms CM-15 (individual) https://www.ksrevenue.gov/pdf/cm15.pdf. Credit card FAQ: https://www.ksrevenue.gov/faqs-credit.html.

entries.name: Boone County Occupational License Department (Kentucky occupational license tax)
entries.service_area_detail: Boone County and cities in the county: occupational license tax on wages and net profits; City of Walton 2% payroll tax from Jan 1, 2026
entries.senior_programs: Kentucky occupational license taxes apply only to wages and business net profits earned in the city or county; Social Security, pensions, IRA distributions, interest and dividends are not taxed, so fully retired people owe nothing. Seniors who are self-employed, do consulting or (in some counties) rent out property may need to file a net profit return.
entries.notes: File and pay through the Boone County Tax Portal (https://boonecounty.munirevs.com/). Net profit returns for calendar-year filers are due April 15. Forms: https://www.boonecountyky.org/services/occupational_licensing/tax_forms/index.php; rates: https://www.boonecountyky.org/services/occupational_licensing/tax_rates/index.php. Office: 2950 Washington Street, Burlington, KY 41005; a new mailing PO box took effect Jan 2, 2026 (use the address on current forms).

entries.name: Campbell County Occupational Tax (Kentucky occupational license tax)
entries.service_area_detail: Campbell County and its cities: occupational license tax on wages and net profits
entries.senior_programs: Kentucky occupational license taxes apply only to wages and business net profits earned in the city or county; Social Security, pensions, IRA distributions, interest and dividends are not taxed, so fully retired people owe nothing. Seniors who are self-employed, do consulting or (in some counties) rent out property may need to file a net profit return.
entries.notes: County occupational tax office for Campbell County, Kentucky.

entries.name: City of Bowling Green Office of Occupational License (Kentucky occupational license tax)
entries.service_area_detail: Bowling Green: 2% occupational license tax on wages and net profits (from Jan 1, 2024)
entries.mail_payment_address: City of Bowling Green, PO Box 1410, Bowling Green, KY 42102-1410
entries.senior_programs: Kentucky occupational license taxes apply only to wages and business net profits earned in the city or county; Social Security, pensions, IRA distributions, interest and dividends are not taxed, so fully retired people owe nothing. Seniors who are self-employed, do consulting or (in some counties) rent out property may need to file a net profit return.
entries.notes: Self-employed individuals file a Net Profit License Fee Return each year; a Net Profit Estimated Payment Form (PDF) and extension request form are on the Office of Occupational License page. Mail: City of Bowling Green, PO Box 1410, Bowling Green, KY 42102-1410.

entries.name: City of Frankfort Licensing Fees (Kentucky occupational license tax)
entries.service_area_detail: Frankfort: occupational license fees on wages and net profits
entries.mail_payment_address: City of Frankfort, P.O. Box 697, Frankfort, KY 40601
entries.senior_programs: Kentucky occupational license taxes apply only to wages and business net profits earned in the city or county; Social Security, pensions, IRA distributions, interest and dividends are not taxed, so fully retired people owe nothing. Seniors who are self-employed, do consulting or (in some counties) rent out property may need to file a net profit return.
entries.notes: Licensing fee payments can be made online through Paymentus. City Hall: 315 W 2nd Street, P.O. Box 697, Frankfort, KY 40601.

entries.name: City of Owensboro Finance Department - Occupational License (Kentucky occupational license tax)
entries.service_area_detail: Owensboro: 1.78% occupational license fee on wages (withheld) and on net profits ($75 minimum)
entries.mail_payment_address: City of Owensboro Finance, 101 East 4th Street, Owensboro, KY 42303
entries.senior_programs: Kentucky occupational license taxes apply only to wages and business net profits earned in the city or county; Social Security, pensions, IRA distributions, interest and dividends are not taxed, so fully retired people owe nothing. Seniors who are self-employed, do consulting or (in some counties) rent out property may need to file a net profit return.
entries.notes: Self-employed people file an annual Net Profit License Fee Return with a copy of their federal return (usually due April 15); an Estimated Payment Voucher form is on the business license page. Office: 101 East 4th Street, Owensboro, KY 42303.

entries.name: City of Richmond Finance Department - License Fee (Kentucky occupational license tax)
entries.service_area_detail: Richmond KY: 2% license fee on net profits (minimum $25) and on wages earned in the city
entries.mail_payment_address: City of Richmond Finance Department, 239 West Main Street, Richmond, KY 40475
entries.senior_programs: Kentucky occupational license taxes apply only to wages and business net profits earned in the city or county; Social Security, pensions, IRA distributions, interest and dividends are not taxed, so fully retired people owe nothing. Seniors who are self-employed, do consulting or (in some counties) rent out property may need to file a net profit return.
entries.notes: Sole proprietors and other businesses file a Net Profit License Fee Return by April 15 (calendar year); only income from work done inside city limits is taxed. Pay by cash, cashier's check, personal check or money order at 239 West Main Street, Richmond, KY 40475. A form to close a business license account is on the Finance pages.

entries.name: Kenton County Occupational License Department (Kentucky occupational license tax)
entries.service_area_detail: Kenton County and participating cities in Kenton County: county and city occupational license fees on wages, net profits and rentals; rates vary by city
entries.mail_payment_address: Kenton County Occupational License, 1840 Simon Kenton Way, Suite 5100, Covington, KY 41011
entries.senior_programs: Kentucky occupational license taxes apply only to wages and business net profits earned in the city or county; Social Security, pensions, IRA distributions, interest and dividends are not taxed, so fully retired people owe nothing. Seniors who are self-employed, do consulting or rent out property in Kenton County may need to file a net profit return.
entries.notes: Anyone doing business, a profession or a rental in Kenton County must file, wherever they live. Use the Community Portal (https://colt.kentoncountyky.gov/) to get a license, file annual and quarterly returns and upload payroll documents; annual returns can also be filed with the Filing Wizard (https://wizard.kentoncountyky.gov/). The portal works best in Google Chrome. You can also file by mail or in person at 1840 Simon Kenton Way, Suite 5100, Covington, KY 41011. Both county and city fees apply where you work.

entries.name: Kentucky Department of Revenue (individual income tax)
entries.service_area_detail: Kentucky individual income tax bills, estimated payments (740-ES), collections balances
entries.phone_pay_by_phone: 502-564-4921 option 1 (Division of Collections; recurring electronic payment plan setup)
entries.mail_payment_address: Bills/estimated payments: KY Department of Revenue, Frankfort, KY 40619-0008 (check payable to "KY State Treasurer")
entries.payment_processor: Kentucky ePayment (https://epayment.ky.gov/EPAY) - bank account or credit card (service provider fees)
entries.senior_programs: Homestead exemption for owners 65+ or totally disabled (Ky. Const. Sec. 170), applied through county PVA; Office of Property Valuation 502-564-8338: https://revenue.ky.gov/Property/Pages/Property-Tax-Exemptions.aspx.
entries.notes: Recurring electronic payment plans for collections balances are set up by calling Division of Collections 502-564-4921 option 1 (per E-file and Payment Options page). Estimated payments page: https://revenue.ky.gov/Individual/Pages/Estimated-Individual-Income-Tax-Payments.aspx. Taxpayer Ombudsman: https://revenue.ky.gov/Get-Help/Pages/Taxpayer-Ombudsman.aspx. Homestead exemption for 65+ is administered by county PVA. To set up a recurring electronic payment plan, call the Division of Collections at 502-564-4921 option 1; use the same number to change or stop it.

entries.name: Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government Division of Revenue (Kentucky occupational license tax)
entries.service_area_detail: Fayette County: 2.25% occupational license fee on wages and net profits earned in Lexington-Fayette County
entries.mail_payment_address: LFUCG Division of Revenue, 218 E. Main St., Lexington, KY 40507
entries.senior_programs: Kentucky occupational license taxes apply only to wages and business net profits earned in the city or county; Social Security, pensions, IRA distributions, interest and dividends are not taxed, so fully retired people owe nothing. Seniors who are self-employed, do consulting or (in some counties) rent out property may need to file a net profit return.
entries.notes: File and pay through the LFUCG Tax Portal (https://lfucg.hylandcloud.com/TaxPortal): estimated net profit payments, extensions, net profit returns and annual returns. Non-residents who worked some days outside the city can request a refund with Form E-1R and employer verification, by email to earningstaxcor@stlouis-mo.gov or fax 314-622-4847, within one year of the due date. The collector's phone line 314-408-6887 takes card payments for water-refuse and real estate only, not earnings tax.

Bank drafts from web applications can be cancelled up to the business day before the draft date if requested by 4:30 p.m. ET (eBusiness Center 5 p.m.); help 1-877-308-9103. Card convenience fee $2 per $100.

entries.name: New York City resident income tax (collected by NY State Department of Taxation and Finance)
entries.parent_company: New York State Department of Taxation and Finance
entries.service_area_detail: New York City residents (all five boroughs) who must file a New York State return; the city tax is reported on Form IT-201 and billed and collected by NY DTF
entries.payment_processor: NY DTF Online Services (bank debit free; card fee via processor)
entries.senior_programs: NYC follows the state rules: Social Security and New York government pensions are not taxed, and up to $20,000 of other pension/annuity income per person 59 1/2 or older is excluded, so many retirees owe little or no city tax.
entries.notes: There is no separate NYC income tax bill: the city tax is part of your New York State return (IT-201), and any bill or notice comes from NY DTF. Pay a bill or notice at https://www.tax.ny.gov/pay/pay-bill.htm; quarterly estimated payments (which include the city tax) at https://www.tax.ny.gov/pay/ind/pay-estimated-tax.htm; review prior estimated payments at https://www.tax.ny.gov/pit/estimated_tax/annual_estimated_tax_account.htm; request an installment payment agreement at https://www.tax.ny.gov/pay/ipa/. Part-year residents use Form IT-360.1. Filed and paid with the New York State return.

Search results  say Online Services has "View and cancel scheduled payments" and phone 518-485-7884. Credit card fee 2.20%.

entries.name: Yonkers resident income tax surcharge and nonresident earnings tax (collected by NY State Department of Taxation and Finance)

entries.senior_programs: Pensions, annuities and government retirement benefits are not taxed. Retired people in a CCA member city who are on file must send an Exemption Certificate instead of a return; it can be filed online at CCA eFile. Individual FAQ: https://www.ccaohio.gov/faq/individual.

Returns with business or rental income (Schedule C/E), K-1s, a refund, or residence tax withheld by an employer must be filed on paper. If you cannot pay, you will receive a billing statement; call CCA to discuss payment arrangements. Accounts referred to the Law Department may qualify for the Selective Intervention Program (S.I.P.) payment plan (https://www.ccaohio.gov/faq/legal). Walk-in and drop box: 205 W St Clair Ave, Cleveland, OH 44113. Forms: https://www.ccaohio.gov/tax-forms.

entries.notes: Pay a tax return balance, quarterly estimate, balance due or extension online through Collector Solutions (https://magic.collectorsolutions.com/magic-ui/Payments/wooster-general/3, the Tax Return Payment link); have your bill or statement in hand. Mail: 538 North Market St., Wooster, OH 44691.

entries.name: Regional Income Tax Agency (RITA) - Ohio municipal income tax
entries.service_area_detail: Municipal income tax for 350+ Ohio member municipalities (local tax, not state)
entries.mail_payment_address: With return: RITA, PO Box 6600, Cleveland, OH 44101-2004; billing statement: RITA, PO Box 94951, Cleveland, OH 44101-4951
entries.payment_processor: RITA MyAccount / FastPay (in-house); card payments carry a 2.75% service charge, ACH free
entries.senior_programs: Social Security, pensions, annuities, IRA and retirement plan distributions, interest, dividends and capital gains are not taxable. A retiree with no taxable income must file an Exemption once, in the first year it applies, online in MyAccount or FastFile or on the paper Exemption Form with page 1 of the federal 1040 attached (forms: https://www.ritaohio.com/Individuals/Home/FormDownloads). Resume filing Form 37 if you later earn wages, self-employment or rental income.
entries.notes: Pay in MyAccount, with FastPay (no account needed: https://eservices.ritaohio.com/webtax/fastpay/home), by phone 24/7 at 800-860-7482, or by mail. Bank account (ACH) and check are free; Visa/Mastercard/Discover add a 2.75% service charge. When mailing a check, always include the bill or statement stub. Mail a return with payment to RITA, PO Box 6600, Cleveland, OH 44101-2004; billing statement payments to RITA, PO Box 94951, Cleveland, OH 44101-4951; payment plan payments to RITA, PO Box 94569, Cleveland, OH 44101-4569. Quarterly estimates (Form 32 EST-EXT) are explained at https://www.ritaohio.com/Individuals/Home/Estimates; estimates cannot go on a payment plan. Balances of $250 or more from a filed return can go on a monthly payment plan set up in MyAccount or by calling ext. 5004; penalty and interest freeze while the plan is current, and AutoPay (bank debit each month) can be turned on in MyAccount for plan payments. Notices (non-filing, subpoena) are explained at https://www.ritaohio.com/Individuals/Home/Notice. Find your town's rate at https://www.ritaohio.com/TaxRatesTable.

entries.name: City of Portland Revenue Division - Arts Education and Access Income Tax (Arts Tax)
entries.service_area_detail: Portland residents 18+ who lived in the city 30+ days and must file an Oregon return; for 2026, $50 single / $100 joint, owed only if Oregon taxable income is over $20,000 single or $40,000 joint
entries.mail_payment_address: Revenue Division, 111 SW Columbia Street, Suite 600, Portland, OR 97201
entries.senior_programs: Social Security, PERS/FERS and other pension and retirement distributions and VA disability do not count as income for the Arts Tax, and households below the income thresholds or the federal poverty level do not owe it.
entries.notes: File and pay online (https://www.portland.gov/revenue/pay-arts-tax), by phone at 503-865-4278, or by mail to Revenue Division, 111 SW Columbia Street, Suite 600, Portland, OR 97201. Due April 15; filing opens in late January. Late payment adds a $15 penalty, plus $20 more if still unpaid after six months.

entries.name: City of Portland Revenue Division - Metro Supportive Housing Services (SHS) and Multnomah County Preschool for All (PFA) personal income taxes

entries.service_area_detail: Metro-area residents and Multnomah County residents with taxable income over $125,000 single / $200,000 joint: Metro SHS 1%; Multnomah PFA 1.5%, plus 1.5% more over $250,000 single / $400,000 joint
entries.senior_programs: Only higher-income households owe these taxes; a senior below the $125,000 single / $200,000 joint thresholds owes nothing.
entries.notes: File at https://www.portland.gov/revenue/file-personal-tax and pay at https://www.portland.gov/revenue/pay-personal-tax or in Portland Revenue Online (https://pro.portland.gov/). Returns are due April 15. Quarterly estimates (April 15, June 15, Sept 15, Jan 15) are required if you expect to owe more than $1,000 ($5,000 starting 2026). Payment plans are available with a $25 setup fee (waived if paid within 12 months).

entries.name: City of Philadelphia Department of Revenue (Wage/Earnings Tax, Real Estate Tax)
entries.service_area_detail: Philadelphia residents and workers (Wage and Earnings Tax, Net Profits Tax) and property owners (Real Estate Tax); also the School Income Tax on residents' unearned income
entries.mail_payment_address: Philadelphia Department of Revenue, P.O. Box 389, Philadelphia, PA 19105-0389 (School Income Tax returns; use the address on your notice for bills)
entries.payment_processor: Kubra EZ-PAY (cards: credit 2.10%, debit $3.45; eCheck free via Philadelphia Tax Center)
entries.senior_programs: Pensions, Social Security and traditional IRA distributions are not subject to the School Income Tax or Wage/Earnings Tax, but interest, dividends and rent are subject to School Income Tax. For senior homeowners: Low-Income Senior Citizen Real Estate Tax Freeze (https://www.phila.gov/services/payments-assistance-taxes/payment-plans-and-assistance-programs/senior-citizen-programs/apply-for-the-low-income-senior-citizen-real-estate-tax-freeze/); Owner-Occupied Real Estate Tax Payment Agreement, OOPA, monthly plan for overdue Real Estate Tax (https://www.phila.gov/services/payments-assistance-taxes/payment-plans-and-assistance-programs/income-based-programs-for-residents/set-up-an-owner-occupied-real-estate-tax-payment-agreement-oopa/); Real Estate Tax Installment Plan for low-income and senior homeowners, apply by end of February (https://www.phila.gov/services/payments-assistance-taxes/payment-plans-and-assistance-programs/income-based-programs-for-residents/set-up-real-estate-tax-installment-plan/); Senior Citizen Water Bill Discount, 25% (https://www.phila.gov/services/payments-assistance-taxes/payment-plans-and-assistance-programs/senior-citizen-programs/apply-for-the-senior-citizen-water-bill-discount/). Senior programs hub: https://www.phila.gov/departments/department-of-revenue/programs/for-senior-citizens/.
entries.notes: File and pay at the Philadelphia Tax Center (https://tax-services.phila.gov/_/); you do not need a username to make a payment or print a voucher. eCheck through the Tax Center is free; cards go through KUBRA EZ-PAY (credit 2.10%, debit $3.45) or by phone at 833-913-0795. Wage Tax is withheld by employers; Earnings Tax (self-employed/non-withheld wages) and School Income Tax returns are due April 15. School Income Tax (3.74% for 2025) applies to residents' dividends, interest, rental income, short-term capital gains, royalties and similar unearned income; mail returns with a printed voucher to Philadelphia Dept. of Revenue, P.O. Box 389, Philadelphia, PA 19105-0389. Payment plans and assistance programs hub: https://www.phila.gov/services/payments-assistance-taxes/payment-plans-and-assistance-programs/.

entries.name: Cumberland County Tax Bureau (Pennsylvania local Earned Income Tax collector)
entries.service_area_detail: Cumberland County Tax Collection District: local Earned Income Tax and Local Services Tax
entries.mail_payment_address: Cumberland County Tax Bureau, 21 Waterford Drive, Suite 201, Mechanicsburg, PA 17050
entries.senior_programs: Pennsylvania local Earned Income Tax does not apply to Social Security, pensions or retirement pay, IRA distributions, interest or dividends. A retiree with no earned income should mark the local return 'retired' (or send the collector a note or retiree statement with the date of retirement) so the collector stops sending returns; if you still work part-time or are self-employed, the tax applies to those earnings.
entries.notes: E-file the EIT return at https://cumberlandtax.rba.com/CCTB/eFilingEntry/eitintroduction.aspx; card payments go through Official Payments with a 3% fee ($1.00 minimum). Self-employed people and others without local withholding who expect $12,000+ of taxable income pay quarterly estimates due April 15, July 15, Oct 15 and Jan 15. Four-month installment plans are available if current-year taxes are up to date; taxes paid after April 15, even on a plan, accrue penalty and interest. Mail: 21 Waterford Drive, Suite 201, Mechanicsburg, PA 17050.

entries.name: EFTPS - Electronic Federal Tax Payment System
entries.parent_company: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Bureau of the Fiscal Service
entries.service_area_detail: Free Treasury payment system for individuals and businesses (estimated taxes, balances due, employment taxes)
entries.notes: Enrollment takes up to 5 business days (PIN mailed). Schedule payments up to 365 days ahead; change or cancel scheduled payments; email notifications; payment history searchable online. Guides: Pub 966 https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p966.pdf. EFTPS page on irs.gov documents scheduling/cancel; eftps.gov is the login site.

entries.name: IRS - Federal individual income tax balance due (Direct Pay / Online Account)
entries.service_area_detail: All U.S. taxpayers; balances due on Form 1040, IRS notices (CP14 etc.), amended returns, extensions
entries.phone_pay_by_phone: Card payments by phone via IRS-approved processors (see pay-by-card page); EFTPS voice response 800-555-3453 for enrolled users
entries.mail_payment_address: Check/money order payable to "U.S. Treasury"; mailing address depends on state and form - see https://www.irs.gov/filing/where-to-file-paper-tax-returns-with-or-without-a-payment
entries.payment_processor: IRS Direct Pay / Online Account (Treasury, free ACH); cards via Pay1040 and ACI Payments (fees apply); cash via retail partners (ACI Payments / Pay1040 barcode)
entries.senior_programs: Tax Counseling for the Elderly (TCE, free tax help age 60+): https://www.irs.gov/individuals/tax-counseling-for-the-elderly; Seniors & retirees hub: https://www.irs.gov/individuals/seniors-retirees; Taxpayer Advocate Service: https://www.taxpayeradvocate.irs.gov/; Offer in Compromise: https://www.irs.gov/payments/offer-in-compromise; Temporarily delay collection (hardship/CNC): https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/temporarily-delay-the-collection-process.
entries.notes: Online Account (sa.www4.irs.gov/ola) shows balance due, payment history (pending, scheduled, canceled, returned, processed) and notices; payments can be scheduled up to 365 days ahead. Direct Pay (https://directpay.irs.gov/directpay/payment) needs no sign-in; one payment at a time (no recurring); scheduled payments can be changed/canceled up to 2 business days before using the confirmation number. There is no ongoing autopay for a one-time balance; recurring automatic payment exists only via a Direct Debit Installment Agreement  or EFTPS scheduling. Card: https://www.irs.gov/payments/pay-your-taxes-by-debit-or-credit-card (to cancel a card payment contact the card processor). Check/money order: https://www.irs.gov/payments/pay-by-check-or-money-order. Cash: https://www.irs.gov/payments/pay-your-taxes-with-cash. Transcripts (account transcript = proof of payments posted): https://www.irs.gov/individuals/get-transcript. Scam note: IRS never demands immediate payment by gift card/wire by phone. IRS pay-by-card page  lists the two authorized card processors: Pay1040 (https://www.pay1040.com/payment/personal; debit $2.15, credit 1.75% min $2.50) and ACI Payments (https://fed.acipayonline.com/index.jsp; debit $2.10, credit 1.85% min $2.50). The page gives no processor phone numbers; card payments are canceled only through the processor.

entries.name: IRS - Payment Plan (Installment Agreement), incl. Direct Debit Installment Agreement
entries.service_area_detail: Monthly installment agreements and short-term (<=180 day) plans for federal tax owed
entries.payment_processor: IRS (Direct Debit from checking; or Direct Pay/EFTPS/card/check monthly)
entries.senior_programs: Low-income setup fee waiver/reduction (Form 13844 https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f13844.pdf); Simple payment plans; Taxpayer Advocate Service.
entries.notes: Online Payment Agreement tool (Apply/Revise) lets you view plan type, due dates and amount, change monthly amount or due date, convert to Direct Debit (the IRS equivalent of autopay), change the bank account, or reinstate after default. Per IRS page (Mar 2026 update): long-term plan via Direct Debit $29 setup fee online (waived for low income); non-direct-debit monthly plan $69 online ($43 low income, may be reimbursed); short-term plan no setup fee. Stopping Direct Debit is done by revising the plan in the same tool or calling.

entries.name: IRS - Quarterly estimated tax payments (Form 1040-ES)
entries.service_area_detail: Retirees with pension/IRA/investment/Social Security income not fully covered by withholding; due Apr 15, Jun 15, Sep 15, Jan 15
entries.payment_processor: IRS Direct Pay / Online Account / EFTPS (free); Pay1040 and ACI Payments for cards
entries.senior_programs: Alternative to quarterly bills: request federal withholding from Social Security (Form W-4V) or pensions/IRA distributions; Tax Withholding Estimator.
entries.notes: Estimated payments can be scheduled in advance: Online Account and Direct Pay allow scheduling up to 365 days ahead; EFTPS allows scheduling up to 365 days in advance and changing/canceling scheduled payments (effectively autopay for all four quarters). Online Account payment history confirms each quarterly payment posted.

entries.service_area_detail: Vermont personal income tax balances, estimated payments, payment plans; Property Tax Credit / Homestead Declaration
entries.payment_processor: myVTax (state) - e-check/ACH debit; card via third-party
entries.senior_programs: Property Tax Credit (income-based, file with Homestead Declaration HS-122): https://tax.vermont.gov/property/tax-credit; myVTax guide: https://tax.vermont.gov/myvtax/homestead-declaration-property-tax-credit; Taxpayer Advocate: https://tax.vermont.gov/help-and-resources/taxpayer-advocate.
entries.notes: Schedule payment for any day up to the due date (Paying Tax Owed page). How to Make a Payment in myVTax: https://tax.vermont.gov/myvtax/make-payment - cancel a payment before 4:00 p.m. ET on business days. Payment options overview: https://tax.vermont.gov/help/payment-options.

entries.name: Washington Department of Revenue (no personal income tax; capital gains excise tax)
entries.service_area_detail: No wage/personal income tax. Capital gains excise tax on high long-term gains; some seniors with large asset sales may owe. Senior property tax exemption/deferral is administered by county assessors/treasurers.
entries.senior_programs: Property tax exemption (age 61+, disabled, or 80%+ disabled veterans; income-based) and deferral (60+) programs, applied through county assessor: https://dor.wa.gov/taxes-rates/property-tax/property-tax-exemptions-and-deferrals.
entries.notes: Included because WA has no personal income tax but does levy a capital gains excise tax: https://dor.wa.gov/taxes-rates/other-taxes/capital-gains-tax. Self-service payment plans with recurring scheduled withdrawals; bank changes at least 2 business days before scheduled payment. Senior Citizen/Disabled property tax exemption is applied for with the county assessor.

entries.name: Wisconsin Department of Revenue (individual income tax)
entries.service_area_detail: Wisconsin individual income tax balances, Form 1-ES estimated payments, payment plans; Homestead Credit (low-income seniors/renters)
entries.mail_payment_address: Use mailing address on the voucher (Customer Service Bureau: PO Box 8949, Madison, WI 53708-8949)
entries.payment_processor: Wisconsin DOR quickpay (https://tap.revenue.wi.gov/pay) - direct debit free; credit card, Apple Pay, PayPal (convenience fees)
entries.senior_programs: Homestead Credit: https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/Individuals/homestead.aspx.
entries.notes: My Tax Account (MTA) lets individuals view mail, schedule and cancel estimated payments, and more (Pay page). Estimated payment voucher 1-ES: https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/OnlineServices/voucher-1es.aspx. Using MTA for personal use FAQ: https://www.revenue.wi.gov/Pages/FAQS/mta-personal.aspx. Payment plan request form A-771. Pay page  confirms My Tax Account can schedule and cancel estimated payments.

entries.name: West Virginia State Tax Department (personal income tax)
entries.service_area_detail: WV personal income tax balances, estimated payments, payment plans; Senior Citizens Tax Credit (property tax) and Social Security modification
entries.payment_processor: MyTaxes (state) - ACH debit ("Pay Personal Income Tax" link); credit cards via third-party (see Credit Card Payments page)
entries.senior_programs: Senior Citizens Tax Credit: https://tax.wv.gov/Individuals/SeniorCitizens/Pages/SeniorCitizensTaxCredit.aspx; Social Security modification: https://tax.wv.gov/Individuals/SeniorCitizens/Pages/SeniorCitizenSocialSecurityModification.aspx; Taxpayer Advocate: https://tax.wv.gov/TaxpayerAdvocate/Pages/TaxpayerAdvocate.aspx.
entries.notes: Payment plans: one-time and recurring payments via MyTaxes; 12-month plan with recurring payments avoids a lien; "Manage Recurring Payments" link on the account controls automatic installment payments (setup/cancel). $15 fee for returned electronic payments. Credit card page: https://tax.wv.gov/Individuals/ElectronicFiling/PaymentOptions/Pages/IndividualsCreditCardPayments.aspx.

entries.name: Wyoming Department of Revenue (no personal income tax)
entries.service_area_detail: No personal income tax
entries.phone_customer_service: 307-777-7320 (Property Tax Refund Program, Department of Revenue)
entries.senior_programs: Wyoming Property Tax Refund Program (income/asset-based refund of property tax on primary residence; online application at https://wptrs.wyo.gov/): https://revenue.wyo.gov/property-tax-refund-program.
entries.notes: No state personal income tax. Property tax is billed by county treasurers; Wyoming property tax refund program for residents is administered by DOR. Property tax relief page  lists the Property Tax Refund Program (annual application, online at wptrs.wyo.gov or through the county treasurer; DOR 307-777-7320) and county property tax deferral.
